title: Did India overestimate anaemia prevalence?
subtitle: Share with anaemia (%). NFHS-5 (2019–21) measured haemoglobin in finger-prick (capillary) blood; ICMR's SAMPADA survey (2023–25) used venous blood and laboratory analysers.
caption: Measured with the gold-standard method, anaemia is lower in every group compared, most of all among young children: 41.8% against 64% in NFHS-5. The gap varies widely, from 25 points for children to one point for women aged 15–49. ICMR cautions that the differences reflect how haemoglobin was measured and should not automatically be read as a fall over time. Either way, anaemia remains widespread: more than half of women and two in five young children.
alt: Dumbbell chart comparing anaemia prevalence in NFHS-5 and SAMPADA. Children 12–59 months: 64% vs 41.8%, 25.2 points lower. Pregnant women: 52% vs 44%, 8 points lower. Men 15–49: 25% vs 19%, 6 points lower. Women 15–49: 57% vs 56%, 1 point lower.
source: ICMR-NIN, SAMPADA 2023–25 fact sheets; PIB release of 23 November 2026 (SAMPADA vs NFHS-5 comparison)

title: Food pushes retail inflation above 6%
subtitle: Consumer price inflation by group, all India, % change on a year earlier, January to October 2026. CPI base 2024=100.
caption: Inflation has risen every month this year, from 2.74% in January to 6.09% in October, above the RBI's 6% upper limit. Food and beverage inflation quadrupled, from 2.11% to 8.51%. Restaurant and hotel prices rose 10.06% on a year earlier and transport 5.84%, after being flat until April. Housing and fuel stayed below 3%.
alt: Line chart of CPI inflation from January to October 2026 for all items and four groups. All items rises from 2.74% to 6.09%; food and beverages from 2.11% to 8.51%; restaurants and accommodation from 2.87% to 10.06%; transport from 0.09% to 5.84%; housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels from 1.47% to 2.90%.
source: MoSPI Consumer Price Index (base 2024=100), all India, rural and urban combined, October 2026 provisional

title: Daily net FPI investment in India, March to November 2026
caption: Foreign portfolio investors pulled money out of India through March and April, turned buyers from late June, sold again from late September into October, and have bought heavily since the start of November.
alt: Bar chart of daily net foreign portfolio investment in India from March to November 2026 in US dollars, with a five-day moving average. Outflows dominate March, April and October; inflows dominate July and November.
source: NSDL FPI Monitor, daily trends in FPI investments, data to 18 November 2026
